title: Posting and Application of Payments on Kestrel Advantage Balloon Contracts
content:
These are the posting and allocation terms of the Kestrel Advantage Balloon Retail Installment Sale Contract.

**1. Payable status.** A payment can be posted only while the contract status is active, assigned for repossession, repossessed or deficiency. *This clause is no longer in force for a return balance payment on a balloon contract in returned status taken under the return balance plan rule, and is superseded by the current basis for that payment; every other payment remains bound by it.* The status is read from the contract record of the contract being paid.

**2. Posting day.** A payment received before the tier's cutoff time, Central Time, on a business day posts that day; a payment received later, or on a weekend or US federal holiday, posts the next business day.

**3. Allocation.** Each payment is applied in the tier's allocation order: first to simple interest accrued over the interest accrual days at the contract APR on the tier's day-basis year, then to principal until the installments due are satisfied, then to fees due, and any remainder to principal. *This clause is no longer in force for a payment the customer makes before a balloon refinance under the pre-refinance payment rule, and is superseded by the current basis for that payment; every other payment keeps this order.*

- The **interest accrual days** are the calendar days from the day after the interest-paid-to date through the payment posting date, both inclusive.
- The **installments due** are the past-due amount plus the monthly payment of the installment due on the next due date when that date falls within one month after the posting date; it is the amount a payment must reach before any part of it goes to fees.
- The interest portion is the lower of the payment and the principal balance times the APR divided by 100 divided by the day basis times the interest accrual days, rounded to the cent. The fee portion is the lower of fees due and whatever of the payment exceeds the higher of the interest portion and the installments due, never below zero. The rest goes to principal.

**4. Fees last.** Because interest is satisfied first and fees last, an installment paid in full within its grace period is never treated as late merely because an earlier fee remains unpaid.

**5. Principal-only payments.** A payment designated principal-only is accepted only when the contract is 0 days past due and is applied to principal after accrued interest is satisfied; it never advances the next due date. Payments in excess of the installment reduce principal and do not advance the next due date unless the customer pays a full additional installment.

**6. Channel fees.** The channel's convenience fee is collected on top of the payment and is never applied to the contract; the agent-assisted debit card fee is not charged when the payment is a reinstatement or redemption, which must be made in certified funds. Debit card payments are limited to the tier's number per calendar month and to the tier's largest single amount each.

**7. Certified funds.** While the certified-funds-only date on the contract is on or after the posting date, only cashier's check, wire or MoneyGram payments are accepted.

**8. Records.** When a payment carries a fee portion, that portion is booked as a fee payment against fees due; enrolling or unenrolling autopay is recorded on the contract.

## Hypothetical allocation (generic figures)

A payment of USD 700.00 posts with USD 90.00 of accrued interest, installments due of USD 550.00 and fees due of USD 40.00. Interest takes USD 90.00; the payment exceeds the higher of 90.00 and 550.00 by USD 150.00, so fees take the lower of 40.00 and 150.00, USD 40.00; principal takes USD 570.00.
